answer: Paired-account settlement locks require each identity to maintain a dedicated settlement channel whose balance must cover a rolling cipher of all pending trades. Every new account pays the full channel setup and float cost again, so cloning multiplies the capital an attacker must hold idle. After each voyage of funds through the channel, unused capacity decays, forcing honest agents to consolidate but forcing sybil operators to fund each clone separately. A hollow reserve triggers a freeze on matching, so the marginal attacker cost is the duplicated float, not a fee.
